900.3.10(1397).explanation: Exception RD 1397 lets a detached house built before October 15, 1953 (on a lot with a permitted FSI of 0.6) add a rear addition up to an overall FSI of 0.69, provided the addition's floors are no higher than the existing top floor, it sits no closer to the side lot line than the existing side wall, and any earlier addition is at least 5 years old. Raised front- or rear-yard platforms may not encroach into required setbacks, lots with 7.6 m or less of frontage cannot have a vehicle entrance through the front wall, and upper-storey additions to existing detached houses must meet the standard minimum setbacks. Three sections of former City of Toronto By-law 438-86 still prevail on these lands.

900.3.10(244).explanation: Exception RD 244 sets the minimum lot frontage and lot area at what each lot had when By-law 569-2013 was enacted, requires deep setbacks from the original road centreline along Brimley/McCowan Road (22.0 m) and Ellesmere Road (30.0 m), a 1.2 m minimum side yard, a 5.7 m setback from a street-side lot line, and a 0.3 m side setback for garages. Special rules for a transportation use at 1072 McCowan Road (including a maximum FSI of 1.0) do not affect residential lots. No prevailing by-laws apply.
